US-CHINA Trade War

By: Julian Sun | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
How the ongoing trade war between The United States & China is impacting ordinary South Africans, especially those with a Huawei

Unique Selling Point:
The American government's blacklisting of Chinese Tech Giant Huawei is the the latest salvo in the ongoing trade war between the The United States & China.

This dispute is having a profound effect on consumers all over the world , including South Africa.

Tonight on Carte Blanche we unpack the trade war, look at its consequences and could portend the start of a new cold war between the World's 2 greatest superpowers.

Summary:
Last week Donald Trump signed an executive order banning American companies from doing business with Chinese tech company Huawei.The telecom giant is the world's second largest smartphone manufacturer. This ban (which goes into effect in 90 days) would see companies like Google & Intel forced into severing ties with Huawei. Right now these phones run the Google Android operating system, as well as apps like Gmail & YouTube.

This would have a direct impact on all South African consumers who own a Huawei phone

The ban is the latest salvo in the ongoing trade war between The United States and China as the 2 superpowers with much at stake. 5G technology looks set to revolutionise the world with the potential to create 3 million jobs in the US and increase GDP by a staggering $500 billion. Right now Huawei has the inside lane to roll out the technology world wide but has been accused of stealing American technology to do so.

Who wins this race has profound consequences for the world and the increasingly acrimonious dispute that has the potential to turn the Cold War of the 21st century

Press Release:


The New Cold War
The battle lines have been drawn – the United States on one end and China on the other. Last week US president Donald Trump signed an executive order banning American companies from doing business with the Chinese tech company Huawei. Now companies like Google and Intel have less than 90 days to sever ties with the cellphone giant. But as the African proverb goes “when elephants fight, it is the grass that suffers” – could South Africa, a BRICS partner, become collateral damage in the escalating trade war between the world’s two largest economies?
Producer: Julian Sun
Presenter: Devi Sankaree Govender


Script:


V/O: The rise of China into a superpower has been remarkable. From an impoverished communist-controlled state a few decades ago, it has transformed into the world’s 2nd largest economy rivalling the United States in power & Influence.

DEVI: Now that rivalry has resulted in a full blown trade war that threatens to destabilise the geopolitical order and herald the start of a new Cold War between East & West with technology on the frontline.

Upsounds of Donald Trump complaining about China

V/O: US President Donald Trump has long complained about China’s trade practices. Last year he imposed tariffs on more than $250 billion worth of Chinese goods sparking the largest trade war in economic history.


Wandile Sihlobo is the chief economist at Agbiz. He explains why the President Trump believes China isn’t playing fair when it comes to trade.

Wandile Sihlobo comment


Now tech companies are in the firing line of an increasingly acrimonious dispute.

LINK: Huawei is the world’s 2nd largest mobile phone manufacturer but its rise to prominence is being viewed as a threat by The United States.

Last week the Trump Administration blacklisted the company, barring American firms like Google, from doing business with the Tech Giant.

V/O: Arthur Goldstuck is one of the foremost tech journalists in the country. He explains why the US chose to black list Huawei in the first place

The US accuse Huawei of being used by the Chinese government to spy on the West

This claim is ludicrous as it would be economic suicide for Huawei

It’s actually because Huawei has become a threat to Apple & Samsung.
V/O: Stuff Magazine editor Toby Shapshak explains the implications of the blacklisting for Huawei

What it means for its relationship with Google, the Android OS and Google Apps like Gmail, YouTube & Google Maps

V/O: Huawei has been given a temporary reprieve through the granting of a 90-day Android licence but what are the consequences for consumers?

Anyone owning a Huawei phone will still enjoy full functionality and updates from Google

It will only impact on future Huawei phones

Huawei have contingency plans with the development of its own OS


V/O: If the US and China are indeed engaged in a technological arms race, what they’re fighting over has the potential to change the world forever.

5G is truly revolutionary and will power the modern 21st century economy by connecting millions of devices at breath-taking speeds. It is up to 20 times faster than 4G and Huawei leads the way when it comes to 5G

Comments about Huawei as market leaders of 5G networks. They are 2 years ahead of their rivals.

The applications of 5G

V/O: Winning the race to roll out 5G would create 3 million jobs in the US and add $500billion to their GDP.

Here in South Africa Rain Mobile is in the process of rolling out one of the first 5G networks in the world .Khaya Dlanga demonstrated how fast 5G really is.

Khaya on Rain’s 5G network and their partnership with Huawei

He also talks about the speed of 5G

On how the blacklisting of Huawei will have no impact on their roll out


V/O: But while the ban will hurt Huawei, it could also cause collateral damage to American tech companies too.

Comments from Arthur, Toby & Brooks


V/O: With trade talks deadlocked it remains to be seen if the blacklisting will be revoked by the Trump Administration.

In the meantime, the Chinese have threatened to block the US from buying rare earth metals according to International Relations expert Brooks Spector
